cities.name: Chicago

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of Cook County, County Department, Probate Division
probateCourt.address: Richard J. Daley Center, 50 West Washington St., Room 1202, Chicago, IL 60602

localNotes: Cook County probate cases are handled by the Probate Division of the Circuit Court, with the clerk's main probate office in Room 1202 of the Richard J. Daley Center, 50 West Washington Street, Chicago. Probate case documents are filed electronically through eFile Illinois (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

A will can be filed with the Probate Division in person at the Daley Center, by mail to the Daley Center, or in person at any of the clerk's five branch offices. The clerk lists no fee for filing a will (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

The Cook County Clerk of the Circuit Court lists a Pro Se/Self-Represented Litigant Center and a guide to free and low-cost legal services in Cook County on its probate page (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

Cook County's recorder of deeds is the Cook County Clerk's Recordings office (312.603.3974). The Clerk's Property After Death resource guide describes the Illinois Transfer on Death Instrument as a single document that moves a home at death, and points to the Clerk's forms page (source: https://cookcountyclerkil.gov/publications/property-after-death-resource-guide). Confirm the recording requirements for your instrument with that office or an attorney.

cities.name: Wheaton

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of the 18th Judicial Circuit (DuPage County), Probate and Guardianship
probateCourt.address: 505 N. County Farm Rd., Wheaton, IL 60187

localNotes: DuPage County's court probate and guardianship page lists the Circuit Court Clerk's Office on the first floor of the courthouse at 505 N. County Farm Rd., Wheaton (630-407-8700), and says guardian reports are e-filed through i2file (source: https://www.dupagecourts.gov/18th_judicial_circuit_court/probate___guardianship/).

The DuPage County Recorder is at 421 N. County Farm Road, Wheaton, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, and accepts documents in person or by mail. This is the office that records a deed or transfer on death instrument for DuPage property (source: https://www.dupageco.org/recorder/).

The DuPage circuit clerk's filing fee book lists no fee to file a will, and a $300 fee to open a decedent's estate, in the schedule effective September 11, 2026. Fees change, so check the current book (source: https://dupagecircuitclerk.gov/18thJudicial/viewstaticpdf?pdfFile=FilingFeesSchedule.pdf).

cities.name: Waukegan

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of the 19th Judicial Circuit (Lake County), Probate Court
probateCourt.address: Lake County Courthouse, 18 N. County St., Waukegan, IL 60085

localNotes: Lake County's probate court sits in the main courthouse at 18 N. County St., Waukegan; the Probate Division's phone is 847-377-3260 (source: https://www.19thcircuitcourt.state.il.us/1331/Probate-Court).

The Lake County probate standing order effective January 12, 2026 requires attorneys and parties to e-file with the Circuit Clerk, and sets hearing days by case type, including Wednesdays for adult guardianships and Fridays for self-represented litigants (source: https://19thcircuitcourt.state.il.us/DocumentCenter/View/5887/DJV-Standing-Order---Procedures-for-Probate-Guardianship-Division-Cases---1-12-26).

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division is at 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan (847-377-2575, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays). Its deed-recording checklist includes any local municipal transfer tax stamp, which must be obtained before submitting a deed (sources: https://www.lakecountyil.gov/Faq.aspx?QID=558 and https://www.lakecountyil.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3233/Pamphlet---Recording-Deeds-PDF).

cities.name: Joliet

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of the 12th Judicial Circuit (Will County)
probateCourt.address: Will County Courthouse, 100 West Jefferson Street, Joliet, IL 60432

localNotes: The 12th Judicial Circuit lists the Will County Courthouse at 100 West Jefferson Street, Joliet (source: https://judges.willcountyillinois.com/Court-Services/Locations).
Will County requires civil e-filing through eFileIL and allows remote video hearings under Administrative Order 2023-2 (source: https://judges.willcountyillinois.com/Circuit-Court).

The Will County Circuit Clerk's fee schedule (effective 07/12/2026, updated 09/03/2026) lists no fee to file a will and a $314 new probate case filing fee. Fees change, so check the current schedule (source: https://www.circuitclerkofwillcounty.com/public-access/fee-schedule).
The Clerk's site offers Zoom virtual court access and a probate forms page (source: https://circuitclerkofwillcounty.com/Court-Forms).

cities.name: Aurora

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of the 16th Judicial Circuit (Kane County), Clerk of the Circuit Court
probateCourt.address: 540 South Randall Road, St. Charles, IL 60174

localNotes: The Kane County Circuit Clerk lists an Aurora Branch in addition to its main office at 540 South Randall Road, St. Charles (630-232-3413). The Aurora Branch is open Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to noon and 1 to 3 p.m., and the clerk's office handles probate and wills for the 16th Judicial Circuit (source: https://cic.countyofkane.org/Pages/contact-us.aspx).
Kane County requires e-filing for new cases unless an Exemption from eFiling for Good Cause applies (source: https://cic.countyofkane.org/Pages/Filing-New-Cases.aspx).
The clerk's fee schedule effective 9/1/2026 lists no fee to file a will and $314 to administer a decedent's estate (source: https://cic.countyofkane.org/Documents/FeeSchedule.pdf).
The clerk's site points self-represented people to the Kane County Law Library & Self Help Legal Center (source: https://cic.countyofkane.org/Pages/Online-Court-Records.aspx).

cities.name: Rockford

The Recorder's Office is at 1504 3rd Avenue, 2nd Floor, in Rock Island. (source: https://rockislandcountyil.gov/308/Recorders-Office)

cities.name: St. Charles

The Kane County Law Library is on the second floor of the Judicial Center, 37W777 IL Route 38, St. Charles. The phone is 630-406-7126. (source: https://www.kclawlibrary.org/Pages/i-am-representing-myself.aspx)

cities.name: Geneva
localNotes: The Kane County Courthouse is at 100 S. Third Street in Geneva. The page does not say which location hears probate. (source: https://www.illinois16thjudicialcircuit.org/Pages/courtAddresses.aspx)

The Kane County Recorder and the Assessment Office are in the Government Center, Building C, 719 S. Batavia Ave., Geneva. (source: https://clerk.kanecountyil.gov/Elections/Documents/GovernmentGuide.pdf)

cities.name: Yorkville
localNotes: The Kendall County Circuit Clerk is at 807 W. John St. in Yorkville. The phone is 630-553-4183. (source: https://www.kendallcountyil.gov/offices/circuit-clerk/probate-deceased)
The Kendall County Recorder's Office is at 502 S. Main St. in Yorkville. The phone is 630-553-4112. (source: https://www.kendallcountyil.gov/offices/county-clerk-recorder)

cities.name: Springfield
localNotes: AgeLinc, the Area Agency on Aging for this region, is at 2731 S. MacArthur Blvd., Springfield, phone (217) 787-9234 or (800) 252-2918. Its site lists help with benefit access and with Medicare Part D enrollment. (source: https://www.agelinc.org)

Land of Lincoln Legal Aid's Northern Regional Office is at 1010 South Second Street, Springfield, phone (217) 529-8400. It lists Sangamon among the counties it serves. (source: https://lincolnlegal.org/locations/)

Sangamon County's Treasurer runs a Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral program for people 65 and older, who may defer all or part of their real estate taxes. (source: https://sangamonil.gov/departments/s-z/treasurer/senior-citizens-real-estate-tax-deferral)

cities.name: Peoria
localNotes: The Peoria Township Assessor is at 427 W. Main Street, Peoria, phone (309) 324-7459, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. The page describes a $5,000 senior exemption at age 65 that requires signing up, and a Senior Assessment Freeze with a $75,000 income limit for 2026. (source: https://peoriatownshipil.com/officials/assessor/)

Central Illinois Agency on Aging, the Area Agency on Aging for Peoria County, is at 700 Hamilton Blvd., Peoria, phone (309) 674-2071. Its site lists information and assistance and Senior Medicare Patrol fraud-prevention outreach. (source: https://www.agecentral.org)

cities.name: Champaign
localNotes: Land of Lincoln Legal Aid's Eastern Regional Office is at 302 North First Street, Champaign, phone (217) 356-1351. It lists Champaign and 14 other counties, including Macon and Vermilion, as its service area. (source: https://lincolnlegal.org/locations/)

The Champaign County Assessment Office, at 102 E. Main Street, Urbana, phone 217-384-3760, offers a $5,000 Senior Homestead Exemption and a Senior Assessment Freeze. (source: https://www.champaigncountyil.gov/ccao/exemptions.php)

cities.name: Bloomington
localNotes: The City of Bloomington Township Assessor is at 607 S. Gridley, Suite A, Bloomington, phone (309) 434-2890. The township office is Suite B, phone 309-434-2730. (source: https://bloomingtoncitytownship.org/services/additional-resources/)

East Central Illinois Area Agency on Aging is at 1003 Maple Hill Road, Bloomington, phone 309-829-2065. It is the Area Agency on Aging for McLean, Champaign, Macon and Vermilion counties, among others. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/forprofessionals/aaa-list.html)

For senior property tax exemptions, call the McLean County Supervisor of Assessments at 309-888-5130. The Treasurer, at 309-888-5180, handles the Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program. (source: https://www.mcleancountyil.gov/406/Senior-Citizen-Tax-Information)

cities.name: Decatur
localNotes: Land of Lincoln Legal Aid has a Decatur office at 1620 South Taylorville Road, phone (217) 859-7320, a satellite of its Champaign office. Its list of counties served includes Macon. (source: https://lincolnlegal.org/locations/)
The Macon County Recorder is at 141 South Main Street, Room 201, Decatur, phone 217-424-1359, and records deeds, mortgages and liens. (source: https://maconcounty.illinois.gov/departments/recorder)

The Macon County Supervisor of Assessments, at 141 South Main Street, Room 401, Decatur, phone 217-424-1364, lists the Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption, the Senior Assessment Freeze and the Senior Tax Deferral program. (source: https://maconcounty.illinois.gov/departments/supervisor-of-assessments/)

cities.name: Quincy
localNotes: The Quincy Township Assessor is at 706 Maine Street, Quincy, phone 217-228-4505, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The page says exemptions are handled by the Adams County Supervisor of Assessments, not the Township Assessor. (source: https://www.quincyil.gov/Government/Quincy-Township/Quincy-Township-Assessor)
Land of Lincoln Legal Aid has a Quincy office at 926 Broadway Street, Suite C, phone (217) 617-4300. It lists Adams among the counties it serves. (source: https://lincolnlegal.org/locations/)

West Central Illinois Area Agency on Aging, the Area Agency on Aging for Adams County, lists a mailing address of 639 York Street, Suite 333, Quincy, phone 217-223-7904. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/forprofessionals/aaa-list.html)

cities.name: Danville
localNotes: CRIS Healthy Aging is at 309 N Franklin Street, Danville, phone (217) 443-2999, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Its site lists Adult Protective Services, Senior Information Services and a Care Coordination Unit for Vermilion County. (source: https://www.agestrong.org)

Call the Vermilion County Assessment Office at 217-554-1940 to have a Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption application mailed to you. (source: https://www.vercounty.org/supervisor-of-assessments/exemption-information/)
The Vermilion County Recorder's standard document fee is $69.00 for deeds, mortgages and releases, effective July 1, 2023. (source: https://www.vercounty.org/recorder/recording-fees/)

cities.name: Elgin
localNotes: Elgin Township's main building is at 729 S. McLean Blvd., Elgin, and its Supervisor's Office can be reached at (847) 741-2045, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The township lists senior programs including a Senior Utility Assistance Application, a Lending Closet and Ride in Kane. (source: https://elgintownship.com/?p=62)

The Illinois Department on Aging senior center list shows Senior Services Associates at 101 South Grove, Elgin, IL 60120, phone 847-741-0404. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

The Kane County senior homestead exemption lowers assessed value by $8,000 for owners age 65 or older. Call the Kane County Assessment Office at 630-208-3818. (source: https://assessments.kanecountyil.gov/Pages/Senior-Homestead.aspx)

cities.name: Edwardsville
localNotes: Edwardsville Township is at 300 W. Park, Edwardsville, IL 62025, phone (618) 656-0292. Its Senior Services Network page, marked coming soon, lists categories such as health insurance and medical assistance, tax relief assistance, elder justice and abuse, and veterans assistance. (source: https://edwardsvilletownship.com/community-services/senior-services)

The Madison County Circuit Clerk's main office is in the Madison County Courthouse at 155 N. Main Street, Edwardsville, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Probate falls under civil cases, which must go through an approved e-filing provider. (source: https://www.madisoncountyil.gov/departments/circuit_clerk/)

Madison County offers a $5,000 Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption for owners age 65 or older. The assessment office phone is (618) 296-6200. (source: https://www.madisoncountyil.gov/departments/chief_county_assesment_office/available_exemptions.php)

cities.name: Carbondale
localNotes: The Illinois Department on Aging lists Senior Adult Services at 409 North Springer Street, Carbondale, IL 62901, phone 618-457-4151. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

The Egyptian Area Agency on Aging, 200 E. Plaza Dr., Carterville, IL 62918, phone (618) 985-8311, serves Jackson County and 12 other southern counties. Its listed services include the Senior Health Insurance Program (SHIP), Adult Protective Services, Legal Assistance and Ombudsman. (source: https://egyptianaaa.org/senior-centers/)

The Jackson County Circuit Clerk is at 1001 Walnut Street, Murphysboro, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., main number (618) 687-7300. Probate is listed as a department you can ask for by phone. (source: https://jacksoncoilcircuitclerk.gov/contact-us/)

cities.name: Kankakee
localNotes: Kankakee County probate filings are handled at the Main Circuit Clerk's Office, Room 209, 450 E. Court Street, Kankakee, IL 60901, phone 815-936-5700. (source: https://kankakeecountyil.gov/502/County-Clerk-of-the-Circuit-Court)

The Supervisor of Assessments is at 189 East Court Street, Kankakee, phone 815-937-2945. Its page lists forms for the general and senior homestead exemptions, the Senior Assessment Freeze (PTAX-340), and the disabled veteran and returning veterans exemptions. The Illinois Department on Aging lists Kankakee County Community Services, Inc. at 657 East Court Street, Kankakee, IL 60901, with a Senior Center line of 815-933-7883. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

cities.name: DeKalb
localNotes: DeKalb Township's Assessor's Office is at 122 North 1st Street, Ste C/D, DeKalb, IL 60115, phone (815) 758-5454, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The page says it can help with information about your property tax assessment. (source: https://dekalbtownship.org/)
The DeKalb Township Supervisor's Office is at 2323 South 4th Street, DeKalb, phone (815) 758-8282, and the township offers help with financial assistance. (source: https://dekalbtownship.org/)

The Illinois Department on Aging lists the DeKalb Senior Citizens Center at 330 Grove Street, DeKalb, IL 60115, phone 815-758-4718. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

cities.name: Crystal Lake
localNotes: The Illinois Department on Aging lists Grand Oaks Active Adults Center at 1401 W. Route 176, Crystal Lake, IL 60014, phone 815-358-2414. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

The City of Crystal Lake's phone list gives the McHenry County Assessments office as (815) 334-4290 and Veteran's Assistance as (815) 334-4229. (source: https://www.crystallake.org/our-community/resident-information/important-phone-numbers-to-know)

McHenry County probate filings must be e-filed unless there is good cause, and wills cannot be e-filed. The original will goes to the Civil windows in Room 136 of the courthouse in Woodstock. (source: https://www.mchenrycircuitclerk.org/court-information/probate/)

cities.name: Downers Grove
localNotes: The Illinois Department on Aging lists the Downers Grove Township Senior Center at 4341 Saratoga Avenue, Downers Grove, IL 60515, phone 630-719-6670. (source: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/aging/resources/documents/seniorcenters.pdf)

The Village of Downers Grove has a full-time Social Worker who can refer residents to services including help with elder abuse, and offers a Senior Resource Guide and a taxi coupon program with a 50% subsidy for eligible participants. (source: https://www.downers.us/socialservicesreferrals)

County Farm Road, Wheaton, and 630-407-5858 is listed for questions about acceptable ownership documents. (source: https://www.dupagecounty.gov/government/departments/supervisor_of_assessments/exemptions/senior_citizens/)
